key_insight: Black participation in landmark hypertrophic cardiomyopathy trials was far below expectation, reaching only about one quarter of the level predicted by the U.S. population, site catchment areas, or disease-based estimates.
clinical_relevance: These enrollment gaps suggest that trial evidence for HCM may not fully reflect the populations most affected, which can limit confidence in how well results generalize across racial groups.
method: Reviewed 197 registered interventional HCM trials and identified 32 landmark-tier studies.
Extracted race data from trials that reported demographics and pooled Black participation using random-effects meta-analysis.
Compared Black enrollment against U.S. population benchmarks, trial site-catchment demographics, and a disease-referenced echocardiographic expectation.
evidence_signal: Across 13 trials with race data, 70 of 1,780 Black or White participants were Black; pooled Black share was 3.98% versus a 16.3% population expectation, with a participation-to-prevalence ratio of 0.24.
watch_item: Not all landmark trials reported race, and the analysis may not capture other structural or operational factors that influenced enrollment beyond geography and eligibility criteria.
paper_title: Race and ethnicity in the landmark hypertrophic cardiomyopathy trials: representation against population, site-catchment, and disease-referenced expectations
